readme.allowed_set_rule: The allowed word set for stage N is the union of decodable_words_introduced and sight_words_introduced for every stage 1..N. Nothing outside that union, plus approved proper nouns, may appear in generated text.
readme.palette_rule: generator_palette is already cumulative and is the ONLY list the story generator may draw content words from. It excludes human nouns and anything frightening. The phonics validator checks against the full allowed set, which is wider - that gap is deliberate, so a child is never failed for a word the generator was allowed to use.
readme.preview_words_rule: At most 1-2 words from stage N+1's decodable_words_introduced may appear in a story, and only if they are also in stage N+1's generator_palette.
readme.proper_nouns: The child's own name and their pet's name are always allowed and are exempt from decodability checks. No other proper nouns are permitted.
readme.caveat: This sequence is a faithful reordering of published sources into ten stages, not a copy of any single published programme. Stage boundaries are editorial. Verify against the cited sources before shipping to children.

sources.title: Suggested Scope & Sequence for Teaching Phoneme-Grapheme Correspondences
sources.used_for: Primary ordering of phoneme-grapheme correspondences. Groups 1-11 map onto stages 1-10 as recorded in each stage's ufli_alignment field.

sources.title: UFLI Foundations Overview
sources.used_for: Programme rationale and the simple-view-of-reading framing behind separating decoding accuracy from comprehension.

sources.title: Letters and Sounds: Principles and Practice of High Quality Phonics (phase structure)
sources.publisher: UK Department for Education, via letters-and-sounds.com and PhonicsPlay subject knowledge notes
sources.used_for: Cross-check on stage boundaries and on the order of consonant digraphs and vowel digraphs. Phase 4 confirms that consonant blends introduce no new correspondences, which is why stage 5 adds structure rather than graphemes.

sources.title: Complete Dolch Word List Divided by Level
sources.publisher: E. W. Dolch, reproduced by CEESA
sources.used_for: Every sight word in this file is drawn from the Dolch pre-primer, primer, grade 1, grade 2 or grade 3 list. The specific list is recorded per word in sight_word_provenance.

sources.title: Fry 1000 Instant Words
sources.used_for: Secondary source for a small number of high-frequency words that are not on any Dolch list (of, other, another, should, water, half, enough, friend, thought, through, different, sure, special, usually, favorite, beautiful).

sources.title: Effect of an Instructional Program in Foundational Reading Skills on Early Literacy Development of Students in Kindergarten and First Grade
sources.publisher: Lane et al., Reading Research Quarterly (2025)
sources.used_for: Efficacy evidence for the UFLI sequence in K and grade 1, the age band this product targets.

is.irregularity: final s says /z/, not taught until stage 3

on.irregularity: regular from stage 2; taught by sight at stage 1 because it is needed sooner

all.irregularity: the 'al' vowel is not the short a taught in stage 1

put.irregularity: u says /oo/ as in book, not short u

some.irregularity: o says /u/; final e is not a long-vowel marker

only.irregularity: o is long inside a closed syllable

both.irregularity: o is long inside a closed syllable

stages.label: Short a and short i, first nine letters
stages.focus: Blending and segmenting VC and CVC words with two vowels and seven consonants.
stages.note: Deliberately the narrowest stage. Expect most children to clear it in under a week. 'is' and 'and' are taught as heart words here because s-as-/z/ and final blends are not introduced until stages 3 and 5.

source_alignment.ufli: Group 1: a, m, s, f, i, p, t, n, d, nasalized a, CVC patterns
source_alignment.letters_and_sounds: Phase 2, Sets 1-2 (s a t p, i n m d). This stage is a superset of the 'satpin' starter set: it adds f and d so that stage 1 yields enough words to build sentences.

stages.label: All five short vowels
stages.focus: Short o, u and e complete the short-vowel set; c, k, b and hard g complete the common single-consonant stops.
stages.note: This is the stage where the vocabulary becomes large enough for real sentences. Cumulative allowed set passes 150 words here.

source_alignment.ufli: Group 2: c (cat), o, k, u, b, g (go), e
source_alignment.letters_and_sounds: Phase 2, Sets 3-4 (g o c k, ck e u r)
source_alignment.deviation: UFLI Group 2 also contains sh and the CCVC/CVCC patterns. We hold sh until stage 4, with the other digraphs, and all consonant blends until stage 5. This keeps stages 1-4 structurally identical - one consonant sound either side of the vowel - so the only thing changing across those four stages is the sound inventory. Letters and Sounds Phase 4 supports treating blends as their own step, since they introduce no new letter-sound correspondences. Verified against UFLI Aug 2026: stage 1 letters match Group 1 exactly; stage 2 matches Group 2 except for the two deferrals named here.

stages.label: Remaining single consonants, floss rule, and ck
stages.focus: h, v, r, l, j, z, w, y, x and qu; s saying /z/ in is, has, his; the floss rule (ff, ll, ss, zz); ck after a short vowel. Plural and third-person -s is available from this stage.
stages.note: Adding -s here is what makes present-tense narration possible.

source_alignment.ufli: Group 3: h, v, r, l, j, z, w/wh, y (consonant), s /z/ (is), ck, ff, ll, ss, zz
source_alignment.letters_and_sounds: Phase 2, Set 5 and Phase 3 single letters (j v w x y z zz qu)

stages.label: Consonant digraphs
stages.focus: sh, ch, th (voiced and unvoiced), wh and ng. Still one consonant sound either side of the vowel, so digraph words are structurally no harder than stage 3 CVC words.
stages.note: Unlocks this, that, them, then, with, which - the connective tissue of narrative prose.

source_alignment.ufli: Group 3 (th, ch, sh, wh) and Group 8 (ng)
source_alignment.letters_and_sounds: Phase 3 consonant digraphs (ch sh th ng)
source_alignment.deviation: sh arrives here rather than in UFLI Group 2, so that all five consonant digraphs are taught together.

stages.label: Consonant blends
stages.focus: Initial and final blends up to three consonants (stop, hand, splash, strong), plus -tch and -dge after a short vowel. Suffix -ing becomes available.
stages.note: The single biggest jump in usable vocabulary. Verbs of motion arrive here, which is when cliffhangers start to work.

source_alignment.ufli: Group 2 (CCVC and CVCC patterns) extended with Group 6 -tch/-dge
source_alignment.letters_and_sounds: Phase 4 - no new letter-sound correspondences, only adjacent consonants
source_alignment.deviation: CCVC and CVCC arrive here rather than in UFLI Group 2. Christine flagged Aug 2026 that 142 new words in one stage is large and that standard practice splits blends into r-, l-, s- and final blends. Deferred to v2: splitting this stage changes every stage number above it and touches progression logic.

stages.label: Silent e and long vowels
stages.focus: a_e, i_e, o_e, u_e and e_e split digraphs. Suffix -ed becomes available, so past-tense narration is possible for the first time.
stages.note: Contrast pairs (cap/cape, hop/hope) are worth surfacing in the story deliberately - they are the point of this stage.

source_alignment.letters_and_sounds: Phase 5 split digraphs (a_e e_e i_e o_e u_e)

stages.label: R-controlled vowels and two-syllable words
stages.focus: ar, or, ore, er, ir and ur. Words may now be two syllables, which brings in the very common -er ending (bigger, winter, ladder).
stages.note: Two syllables is a real cognitive step. Hold sentence length steady for a session or two after a child arrives here.

source_alignment.ufli: Group 4 (ar, or, er) and Group 5 (ir, ur, closed and open syllables, multisyllable words)
source_alignment.letters_and_sounds: Phase 3 (ar or ur er) and Phase 5

stages.label: Long vowel teams
stages.focus: ai, ay, ee, ea, oa, ow (as in snow), igh, and y saying /E/ (happy) or /I/ (cry). Suffixes -er and -est become available.
stages.note: Largest single vocabulary addition in the sequence. Adjectives finally become plentiful, which is what makes descriptions land.

source_alignment.ufli: Group 4 (ai, ay, ee, ea) and Group 5 (oa, ow, y as a vowel)
source_alignment.letters_and_sounds: Phase 3 (ai ee igh oa) and Phase 5 (ay ea)

new_graphemes.phoneme: /E/ at end of a longer word
/I/ at end of a short word

stages.label: Diphthongs and other vowel teams
stages.focus: oo (both sounds), ou, ow (as in cow), oi, oy, aw, au, ew, ie, ear and air.
stages.note: Note that ow and oo each have two sounds. The audio engine should expect either pronunciation on first attempt.

source_alignment.ufli: Group 6 (ou, ow, oi, oy, oo, ie) and Group 8 (ew, au, aw)
source_alignment.letters_and_sounds: Phase 3 (oo ow oi ear air) and Phase 5 (ou ie oy aw ew)

stages.label: Multisyllable words, soft c and g, silent letters
stages.focus: Open syllables (robot, paper), the final stable syllable -le (apple, turtle), soft c and g (city, gem), kn, wr and ph, compound words, and up to three syllables.
stages.note: End of the intended range. A child reading fluently at stage 10 is decoding at roughly end-of-first-grade level and has outgrown this product's ceiling.

source_alignment.ufli: Group 5 (open syllables), Group 7 (c and g before i/e/y), Group 11 (wr, kn, ph)
